findings.class: failure path / loud-and-typed: a ring named by path runs its probes with no grant
findings.where: scripts/orchflows_check.py `_untrusted` (6bd287a9): returns the ring only when it is the project ring and the ledger does not trust it; `ring_at` admits any directory
findings.evidence: Probe P4: `orchflows check <dir>` on a scratch directory that is neither the home ring nor any project's `.orchflows` -- the shape of a bundle someone just cloned to look at -- ran the `tools.txt` probe (marker file written) and exited 0 with no trust sentence. B1.22's holding for this verb was 'grading needs no trust grant, which is right for a read-only verdict'; this artifact makes grading run item content on every ring except an untrusted project ring. The executor reported the same as uncovered and asked for a ruling. rings._trust_state has no cell for a path-named ring (home/imports/library inherent, project held to the ledger), so the artifact's reading of the law is defensible; the failure path is nonetheless unstated in the spec and unchecked.
findings.why_not_blocking: no frozen criterion names it (spec section 2 says 'or the directory given' and is silent on trust); the fixed acceptance and its stated failure paths hold; rules/verification.md section 10.
findings.smallest_change: invert the question in `_untrusted`: probe only where the ring is the home ring, sits under the home ring's imports directory, or is a project ring the ledger trusts; every other directory takes the same UNTRUSTED_REMEDY WARN (remedy `orchflows trust <dir>`, which the ledger keys by bundle path). One function and one check mirroring test_an_untrusted_project_ring_gets_the_remedy_and_runs_no_probe over a path-named ring.
